prompt: Consider a community that requires all members to perform compulsory labor for communal projects, punishing refusal with exile. The community claims its standards define acceptable contribution and justify the punishment. An external critic argues that this forced‑labor punishment violates the right to freedom of work, yet maintains that no neutral moral authority exists beyond competing cultural preferences. Is the claim that condemning this punishment as a rights violation objectively binding? Answer with a single word ('Yes' or 'No').

There is no external rulebook translating those uses into one master standard. Decide whether universal condemnation of a harmful practice therefore lacks objective authority beyond a competing form of life, and apply the verdict to an injury case.
